choices.feedback: Forget debit cards and credit cards. Debit/credit are sides of the accounting system; the effect depends on account type.

data.title: Debit vs. credit effects
data.prompt: Which side increases an Asset?

choices.feedback: Assets increase with debits.

data.title: Debit vs. credit effects
data.prompt: Which side decreases an Asset?

choices.feedback: Assets decrease with credits.

data.title: Debit vs. credit effects
data.prompt: Which side increases a Liability?

choices.feedback: Liabilities increase with credits.

data.title: Debit vs. credit effects
data.prompt: Which side decreases a Liability?

choices.feedback: Liabilities decrease with debits.

data.title: Debit vs. credit effects
data.prompt: Which side increases Common Stock?

choices.feedback: Common Stock is equity and normally increases with a credit.

data.title: Debit vs. credit effects
data.prompt: Which side increases Retained Earnings?

choices.feedback: Retained Earnings is equity and normally increases with credits.

data.title: Debit vs. credit effects
data.prompt: Which side increases Service Revenue?

choices.feedback: Revenues increase with credits.

data.title: Debit vs. credit effects
data.prompt: Which side increases Rent Expense?

choices.feedback: Expenses increase with debits.

data.title: Debit vs. credit effects
data.prompt: Which side increases Dividends?

choices.feedback: Dividends reduce equity and carry a normal debit balance.

data.title: Debit vs. credit effects
data.prompt: Does a debit increase or decrease Cash?

choices.feedback: Cash is an asset, so a debit increases it.

data.title: Debit vs. credit effects
data.prompt: Does a credit increase or decrease Accounts Receivable?

choices.feedback: Accounts Receivable is an asset, so a credit decreases it.

data.title: Debit vs. credit effects
data.prompt: Does a debit increase or decrease Accounts Payable?

choices.feedback: Accounts Payable is a liability, so a debit decreases it.

data.title: Debit vs. credit effects
data.prompt: Does a credit increase or decrease Unearned Revenue?

choices.feedback: Unearned Revenue is a liability, so a credit increases it.

data.title: Debit vs. credit effects
data.prompt: Does a debit increase or decrease Equipment?

choices.feedback: Equipment is an asset, so a debit increases it.

data.title: Debit vs. credit effects
data.prompt: Does a credit increase or decrease Accumulated Depreciation?

data.title: Debit vs. credit effects

data.title: Statement classification
data.prompt: Which financial statement reports Revenues and Expenses?

choices.feedback: Revenues and expenses belong on the income statement.

data.prompt: Which financial statement reports Assets, Liabilities, and Equity?

choices.feedback: The balance sheet is the A = L + E statement.

data.title: Statement classification
data.prompt: Which statement does Cash go on?

choices.feedback: Cash is an asset, so it appears on the balance sheet.

choices.text: Both income statement and retained earnings

data.title: Statement classification
data.prompt: Which statement does Accounts Payable go on?

choices.feedback: Accounts Payable is a liability, so it appears on the balance sheet.

data.title: Statement classification
data.prompt: Which statement does Common Stock go on?

choices.feedback: Common Stock is equity and appears on the balance sheet.

data.title: Statement classification
data.prompt: Which statement does Service Revenue go on?

choices.feedback: Revenue appears on the income statement.

choices.text: Both balance sheet and retained earnings

data.title: Statement classification
data.prompt: Which statement does Rent Expense go on?

choices.feedback: Expenses appear on the income statement.

data.title: Statement classification
data.prompt: Which statement does Accumulated Depreciation go on?

data.title: Statement classification
data.prompt: Which statement does Dividends go on in this intro-statement sequence?

choices.feedback: Dividends are not an expense. They reduce retained earnings and appear in the retained-earnings calculation.

data.title: Statement classification
data.prompt: Where does ending Retained Earnings appear?

data.prompt: Which statement does Unearned Revenue go on?

data.title: Statement classification

data.title: Statement classification
